title: Microsoft Agent 365: the control plane for agents
summary: The assurance that agents keep running unchanged if administrators do nothing is not established by the documentation checked. The control paths, API references and per-user prices are supported; the briefing also correctly reports disagreements in Microsoft's licensing and registry documentation.

claims.quote: Agent 365 is the control plane for AI agents. It empowers IT and security administrators to observe, govern, and secure agents across Microsoft 365 and connected platforms at scale.

claims.claim: The All agent identities policy targets Entra agent identity authentication, not arbitrary registry entries without that identity type.
claims.quote: Conditional Access enforcement applies when an agent identity or agent's user account requests a token for any resource. It does not apply when an agent identity blueprint acquires a token to create agent identities or agent's user accounts.

claims.claim: A tenant-wide Conditional Access block prevents existing and new agent identities from authenticating.
claims.quote: Applying the policies prevents existing and new agent identities from authenticating, but it doesn't prevent the creation of agent identities in your tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft cautions that globally disabling agent identities can cause existing agents to fail.
claims.quote: Globally disabling agent identities can cause existing agents to fail, degrade Microsoft product experiences, and push teams to use less transparent application or service principal identities.

claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning "If nobody acts" with: "The licensing FAQ includes the registry with a Microsoft cloud subscription; premium governance, observability and security capabilities require Agent 365." The enablement prerequisite does not establish that existing agents and their operation remain unchanged.
